subproblems.title: Mass representation and restrictions of currents with locally finite mass (Simon 6.2.7–2.9)
subproblems.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and every X ∈ D_k(U) with M_W(X) < ∞ for every open W whose closure is a compact subset of U, there are a Borel measure μ on ℝ^P and v : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (k-vectors, i.e. continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) such that: (a) IsMeasureRepresentation X μ v, i.e. for every test form ω ∈ D^k(U) the function x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and X(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x); (b) μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0; (c) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; (d) |v(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every x ∈ ℝ^P and every k-covector α, where |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm); (e) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P there is S ∈ D_k(U) with S(ω) = ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω ∈ D^k(U); (f) for every Borel A, every S ∈ D_k(U) with S(ω) = ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω, and every open W ⊆ U, M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A) in [0,∞].

subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions (as in the parent proof). D^k(U) is the space of test k-forms on U (smooth, compact support, tsupport ⊆ U; `TestFormOn U k`), D_k(U) the currents (`GeometricCurrentOn U k`: linear, and X(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in D^k(U), i.e. all tsupports lie in one compact K ⊆ U and every iterated derivative of ω_j tends to 0 uniformly on K). I(k,P) is the set of strictly increasing β : {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; e_β := (e_{β_1},…,e_{β_k}); dx^β is the coordinate k-covector, dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ} for β, γ ∈ I(k,P). Fact A: every k-covector α equals Σ_β α(e_β) dx^β, and |α|² = Σ_β α(e_β)², where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. A k-vector is a continuous linear functional w on k-covectors (`NVector`); put w^β := w(dx^β), so w(α) = Σ_β α(e_β) w^β and |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w| with |w| := (Σ_β (w^β)²)^{1/2} (Cauchy–Schwarz). For a form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of X(ω) over ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. ρ_ε is a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, supported in the closed ε-ball, ∫ρ_ε = 1); for a continuous compactly supported form φ, ρ_ε*φ (componentwise convolution) is smooth, supported in the closed ε-neighbourhood of tsupport φ, satisfies |ρ_ε*φ(x)| ≤ ‖φ‖ (|·| is a norm, hence convex) and ρ_ε*φ → φ uniformly as ε ↓ 0. All measures are Borel measures on ℝ^P = Eucl P.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14 (Riesz) and Theorem 1.17 (Lusin). This is the parent proof's preliminaries R0, R1, R1′ and R3, specialized to the statement. Let P, k, U open and X ∈ D_k(U) with M_W(X) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure ⊆ U.

1. (Mass estimate, R0.) If ω ∈ D^k(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then |X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X)‖ω‖ (in [0,∞]). Indeed, if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0 and X(ω) = 0; otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ are admissible for M_W(X), so ±X(ω)/‖ω‖ ≤ M_W(X).

2. (Extension to continuous forms.) Let H := ℝ^{I(k,P)} with the Euclidean inner product ⟨·,·⟩_H and J : α ↦ (α(e_β))_β, a linear isometry of (k-covectors, |·|) onto H (Fact A). Let C_c(U;H) be the continuous maps U → H with compact support in U; identify φ ∈ C_c(U;H) with the continuous k-form on ℝ^P equal to J⁻¹φ on U and 0 off U (continuous because its support is a compact subset of the open set U). For φ ∈ C_c(U;H) with K := tsupport φ choose r > 0 such that the closed 2r-neighbourhood of K lies in U, and let W_K := {x : dist(x,K) < 2r}; W_K is open with compact closure ⊆ U, so M_{W_K}(X) < ∞. For 0 < ε < r, φ_ε := ρ_ε*φ ∈ D^k(U), tsupport φ_ε ⊆ W_K and φ_ε → φ uniformly. By step 1, |X(φ_ε) − X(φ_δ)| ≤ M_{W_K}(X)‖φ_ε − φ_δ‖ → 0, so X̄(φ) := lim_{ε↓0} X(φ_ε) exists. Two families of test forms supported in a common open set with compact closure in U and converging uniformly to φ have X-values whose difference tends to 0 (step 1 again), so X̄(φ) does not depend on r or on the mollifier. X̄ is linear (ρ_ε*(aφ+bψ) = aρ_ε*φ + bρ_ε*ψ), X̄(ω) = X(ω) for ω ∈ D^k(U) (ρ_ε*ω → ω uniformly with supports in a fixed W_K), and |X̄(φ)| ≤ M_{W_K}(X)‖φ‖ whenever tsupport φ ⊆ K (because ‖φ_ε‖ ≤ ‖φ‖). Hence for every compact K ⊆ U, sup{X̄(φ) : φ ∈ C_c(U;H), |φ| ≤ 1, tsupport φ ⊆ K} < ∞.

3. (Riesz representation on U, R1.) U with the subspace topology is a locally compact Hausdorff space and H is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space. By step 2, X̄ satisfies the hypothesis of the Riesz Representation Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14; in the pinned library `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_14`, with hypothesis `IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional`). Hence there are a Radon measure μ_U on U (Borel regular, finite on compact subsets of U) and a μ_U-measurable ν : U → H with |ν| = 1 μ_U-a.e. and X̄(φ) = ∫_U ⟨φ(x), ν(x)⟩_H dμ_U(x) for all φ ∈ C_c(U;H). Since U is σ-compact and μ_U is finite on compact subsets of U, μ_U is σ-finite; being Borel regular, every μ_U-measurable set differs from a Borel set by a μ_U-null set, so ν agrees μ_U-a.e. with a Borel map ν₀. Put ν₁(x) := ν₀(x) if |ν₀(x)| = 1 and ν₁(x) := 0 otherwise. Then ν₁ is Borel, |ν₁| ≤ 1 everywhere, ν₁ = ν and |ν₁| = 1 μ_U-a.e. Below μ_U denotes the restriction of the Radon measure to the Borel subsets of U.

4. (Extension by zero to ℝ^P; conclusions (a)–(d).) Define μ(B) := μ_U(B ∩ U) for Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P (the push-forward of μ_U under the inclusion U ↪ ℝ^P, which is Borel since U is open). For x ∈ U let v(x) be the k-vector α ↦ ⟨Jα, ν₁(x)⟩_H, and let v(x) := 0 for x ∉ U (a linear functional on a finite-dimensional space, hence continuous). Then:
 (b) μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = μ_U(∅) = 0.
 (c) If K ⊆ U is compact, K is a compact subset of U and μ(K) = μ_U(K) < ∞.
 (d) |v(x)(α)| ≤ |Jα|·|ν₁(x)| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Schwarz; 0 off U). Moreover v(x)^β = ν₁^β(x), so |v(x)| = 1 for μ-a.e. x.
 (a) Let ω ∈ D^k(U) and K := tsupport ω (compact, ⊆ U). The function x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) = 1_U(x)⟨Jω(x), ν₁(x)⟩_H is Borel, vanishes off K and is bounded by ‖ω‖, and μ(K) < ∞, so it is μ-integrable; and ∫ v(ω) dμ = ∫_U ⟨Jω, ν₁⟩_H dμ_U = ∫_U ⟨Jω, ν⟩_H dμ_U = X̄(ω|_U) = X(ω). Hence IsMeasureRepresentation X μ v.
 (R1′: no finiteness of μ on compact subsets of ℝ^P meeting ∂U is claimed or used; e.g. for P = 1, U = (0,1), X(a dx) := ∫_0^1 a(x)x⁻¹dx one has M_W(X) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U but μ([0,1]) = ∞.)

5. (Restrictions are currents, conclusion (e), Simon 2.9.) Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and S(ω) := ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for ω ∈ D^k(U); by (a) the integrand is integrable, so S is a well-defined linear functional. If ω_j → 0 in D^k(U), there is a compact K ⊆ U containing every tsupport ω_j with ω_j → 0 uniformly on K (zeroth iterated derivative); by (d), |S(ω_j)| ≤ ∫_K |ω_j(x)| dμ ≤ μ(K)·sup_K |ω_j| → 0, since |·| is a norm on the finite-dimensional space of k-covectors (hence bounded by a constant times the operator norm) and μ(K) < ∞ by (c). Thus S ∈ D_k(U) and S(ω) = ∫_A v(ω) dμ for every ω.

6. (Mass of restrictions, conclusion (f), R3.) Let A be Borel, S ∈ D_k(U) with S(ω) = ∫_A v(ω) dμ for all ω, and W ⊆ U open.
 (≤) If ω is admissible for M_W(S) (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1), then by (d) S(ω) ≤ ∫_A |v(x)(ω(x))| dμ ≤ μ(A ∩ tsupport ω) ≤ μ(W ∩ A). Taking the supremum, M_W(S) ≤ μ(W ∩ A).
 (≥) Let 0 ≤ c < μ(W ∩ A) and η > 0. (i) Choose compacts K_j with K_j ⊆ int K_{j+1} and ⋃_j K_j = U. Each μ⌞K_j is a finite Borel measure on the Polish space ℝ^P, hence inner regular by compact sets, and μ(W ∩ A ∩ K_j) ↑ μ(W ∩ A); so there is a compact C ⊆ W ∩ A with c < μ(C) < ∞. (ii) N := {x : |v(x)| ≠ 1} is a μ-null Borel set. By Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17, applied to the finite Borel measure μ⌞C and the Borel functions v^β) and inner regularity there is a compact C′ ⊆ C ∖ N with μ(C ∖ C′) < η such that every v^β is continuous on C′. (iii) Y(x) := Σ_β v(x)^β dx^β (x ∈ C′) is a continuous covector field on C′ with |Y(x)| = 1 and v(x)(Y(x)) = Σ_β (v(x)^β)² = 1. By Tietze's theorem (applied to the coefficients) Y extends to a continuous Ỹ on ℝ^P; replacing Ỹ by π∘Ỹ with π(y) := y/max(1,|y|) (continuous, |π(y)| ≤ 1, π(y) = y for |y| ≤ 1) we may assume |Ỹ| ≤ 1, still Ỹ = Y on C′. (iv) Choose r₀ > 0 with the closed 2r₀-neighbourhood of C′ inside W. The open sets O_j := {dist(·,C′) < r₀/j} decrease to the closed set C′ and μ(O_1) ≤ μ({dist(·,C′) ≤ r₀}) < ∞ (compact ⊆ U), so there is an open O ⊇ C′ with closure O ⊆ {dist(·,C′) ≤ r₀} and μ(O ∖ C′) < η. Let ψ be continuous with 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on C′, tsupport ψ ⊆ O (Urysohn), and φ := ψỸ. Then φ is a continuous form with compact support in W, |φ| ≤ 1, and, since C′ ⊆ C ⊆ A, v(φ) = 1 on C′, |v(φ)| ≤ 1 on O ∖ C′ (by (d)) and φ = 0 off O:
 ∫_A v(φ) dμ ≥ μ(C′) − μ(O ∖ C′) ≥ μ(C) − 2η.
 (v) For 0 < ε < r₀, φ_ε := ρ_ε*φ ∈ D^k(U) has tsupport in the compact set K′ := {dist(·,C′) ≤ 2r₀} ⊆ W, |φ_ε| ≤ 1 and φ_ε → φ uniformly; thus φ_ε is admissible for M_W(S) and, by dominated convergence (|v(φ_ε)| ≤ 1_{K′}, μ(K′) < ∞), S(φ_ε) → ∫_A v(φ) dμ. Hence M_W(S) ≥ μ(C) − 2η > c − 2η. As c < μ(W ∩ A) and η > 0 are arbitrary, M_W(S) ≥ μ(W ∩ A).
 Therefore M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A) in [0,∞].

7. (Conclusion.) The pair (μ, v) of step 4 satisfies (a) IsMeasureRepresentation X μ v, (b) μ Uᶜ = 0, (c) μ K < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, (d) |v x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for all x, α, (e) existence of the restriction currents (step 5) and (f) the mass formula (step 6). ∎
proof_key_steps: Mass estimate |X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X)‖ω‖ for tsupport ω ⊆ W (R0).
Extend X by mollification to a locally bounded linear functional X̄ on C_c(U; H), H = ℝ^{I(k,P)} ≅ Λ^k with the Euclidean coefficient norm.
Riesz (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14 / SimonGMT simon_theorem_4_14) on the locally compact space U: Radon μ_U and unit field ν; replace ν by a Borel field ν₁ with |ν₁| ≤ 1 everywhere, = 1 a.e.
Extend by zero: μ(B) = μ_U(B ∩ U), v = 0 off U; get the representation, μ Uᶜ = 0, finiteness on compacts of U and |v x α| ≤ |α|.
Restrictions ∫_A v(ω) dμ are sequentially continuous (dominated by μ(K) sup_K |ω_j|), hence currents.
M_W(X⌞A) ≤ μ(W∩A) by (d); ≥ by inner regularity, Lusin, Tietze, Urysohn and mollification.

Source: the parent proof's preliminary R2 (uniqueness in Simon 2.7–2.9), stated locally on an open set W. Let P, k, U open, Borel measures μ₁, μ₂ on ℝ^P and maps v₁, v₂ : ℝ^P → (k-vectors) be such that x ↦ v_i(x)(ω(x)) is μ_i-integrable for every ω ∈ D^k(U) (i = 1, 2). Let W be open with ∫ v₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫ v₂(ω) dμ₂ for all ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Write v_i^β(x) := v_i(x)(dx^β). Fix a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P and ω ∈ D^k(U) with K := tsupport ω ⊆ W.

1. (A neighbourhood of K.) K is compact and K ⊆ W ∩ U (test forms on U have tsupport ⊆ U), and W ∩ U is open. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and both sides vanish; assume K ≠ ∅. Choose r > 0 such that the closed 2r-neighbourhood of K lies in W ∩ U; put W′ := {x : dist(x,K) < r} (open) and K_r := {x : dist(x,K) ≤ r} (compact, ⊇ closure W′, ⊆ W ∩ U).

2. (Local integrability.) Fix β ∈ I(k,P). Choose a smooth χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K_r and tsupport χ a compact subset of {dist(·,K) < 2r} ⊆ W ∩ U, e.g. a mollified indicator function. The form x ↦ χ(x)dx^β is smooth with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, i.e. it belongs to D^k(U); hence x ↦ v_i(x)(χ(x)dx^β) = χ(x)v_i^β(x) is μ_i-integrable. Therefore g_i^β := 1_{K_r}·v_i^β = 1_{K_r}·(χv_i^β) is μ_i-integrable (it is a.e.-strongly measurable as the product of an integrable function with the indicator of a closed set, and |g_i^β| ≤ |χv_i^β|).

3. (Agreement on smooth functions.) If φ is smooth with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ W′, then φdx^β ∈ D^k(U) has tsupport ⊆ W′ ⊆ W, so by hypothesis ∫ φv₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φv₂^β dμ₂, i.e. ∫ φ g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂^β dμ₂ (φ vanishes off W′ ⊆ K_r).

4. (Agreement on continuous functions.) Let φ be continuous with compact support tsupport φ ⊆ W′, and s := dist(tsupport φ, ℝ^P ∖ W′) > 0 (s := 1 if W′ = ℝ^P). For 0 < ε < s/2, φ_ε := ρ_ε*φ is smooth with tsupport ⊆ {dist(·, tsupport φ) ≤ ε} ⊆ W′, |φ_ε| ≤ sup|φ|, and φ_ε → φ uniformly. By step 3, ∫ φ_ε g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φ_ε g₂^β dμ₂; dominated convergence (dominating functions sup|φ|·|g_i^β|) gives ∫ φ g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂^β dμ₂.

5. (Equality of measures on W′.) Define finite Borel measures λ₁(B) := ∫_B (g₁^β)⁺ dμ₁ + ∫_B (g₂^β)⁻ dμ₂ and λ₂(B) := ∫_B (g₁^β)⁻ dμ₁ + ∫_B (g₂^β)⁺ dμ₂. Step 4 says ∫ φ dλ₁ = ∫ φ dλ₂ for every continuous φ with compact support in W′. (i) For open O ⊆ ℝ^P, V := O ∩ W′ is open and φ_j(x) := min(1, max(0, j·dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) − 1))·max(0, min(1, j − |x|)) are continuous, compactly supported in V, 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1, and φ_j ↑ 1_V pointwise (if V = ℝ^P, which is possible only for P = 0, take the first factor ≡ 1); by monotone convergence λ₁(O ∩ W′) = λ₂(O ∩ W′). (ii) The finite measures B ↦ λ_i(B ∩ W′) agree on the π-system of open sets, which generates the Borel σ-algebra and contains ℝ^P; by the π–λ uniqueness theorem they agree on all Borel sets.

6. (Bounded Borel integrands.) Consequently ∫ h dλ₁ = ∫ h dλ₂ for every bounded Borel h vanishing off W′ (apply step 5 to simple functions and pass to uniform limits, separately for h⁺ and h⁻). Expanding λ₁, λ₂ (all terms are finite since g_i^β is integrable and h bounded) gives ∫ h g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ h g₂^β dμ₂.

7. (Conclusion.) By Fact A, ω(x) = Σ_β ω_β(x) dx^β with ω_β(x) := ω(x)(e_β) continuous and vanishing off K ⊆ W′. Hence 1_A(x)v_i(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_β h_β(x) g_i^β(x) with h_β := 1_A ω_β, a bounded Borel function vanishing off K (on K ⊆ K_r, v_i^β = g_i^β). By step 6 for each β,
 ∫_A v₁(ω) dμ₁ = Σ_β ∫ h_β g₁^β dμ₁ = Σ_β ∫ h_β g₂^β dμ₂ = ∫_A v₂(ω) dμ₂.
 This holds for every Borel A and every ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. (Special cases used by the siblings: W = ℝ^P gives uniqueness of restrictions — two representations of the same current have the same restrictions; μ₂ = 0, v₂ = 0 gives locality — if ∫ v₁(ω) dμ₁ = 0 for all ω supported in W, then ∫_A v₁(ω) dμ₁ = 0 for all such ω.) ∎

Testing with χ dx^β (χ = 1 near K) shows g_i^β = 1_{K_r} v_i(dx^β) ∈ L¹(μ_i).
The hypothesis with φ dx^β gives ∫ φ g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂^β dμ₂ for smooth φ supported in W′; extend to continuous φ by mollification and dominated convergence.

subproblems.title: Existence of the slices ⟨T,f,t₋⟩ (Simon 4.6)
subproblems.statement: For all P, m, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞ for all open W ⊂⊂ U, every f : ℝ^P → ℝ which is L-Lipschitz on U and every t ∈ ℝ, there is S ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t S, i.e. S = ∂(T⌞{x ∈ U : f(x) < t}) − (∂T)⌞{x ∈ U : f(x) < t} for some restriction currents in the sense of IsRestriction.

Conventions (as in the parent proof). D^k(U) is the space of test k-forms on U (smooth, compact support, tsupport ⊆ U; `TestFormOn U k`), D_k(U) the currents (`GeometricCurrentOn U k`: linear, and X(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in D^k(U), i.e. all tsupports lie in one compact K ⊆ U and every iterated derivative of ω_j tends to 0 uniformly on K). I(k,P) is the set of strictly increasing β : {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; e_β := (e_{β_1},…,e_{β_k}); dx^β is the coordinate k-covector, dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ} for β, γ ∈ I(k,P). Fact A: every k-covector α equals Σ_β α(e_β) dx^β, and |α|² = Σ_β α(e_β)², where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. A k-vector is a continuous linear functional w on k-covectors (`NVector`); put w^β := w(dx^β), so w(α) = Σ_β α(e_β) w^β and |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w| with |w| := (Σ_β (w^β)²)^{1/2} (Cauchy–Schwarz). For a form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of X(ω) over ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. ρ_ε is a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, supported in the closed ε-ball, ∫ρ_ε = 1); for a continuous compactly supported form φ, ρ_ε*φ (componentwise convolution) is smooth, supported in the closed ε-neighbourhood of tsupport φ, satisfies |ρ_ε*φ(x)| ≤ ‖φ‖ (|·| is a norm, hence convex) and ρ_ε*φ → φ uniformly as ε ↓ 0. Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.6 and the parent proof's Step 1, using the sibling `slicing_mass_representation` (R1/R3) in place of the parent's preliminaries. Let P, m, U open, T ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure ⊆ U, f : ℝ^P → ℝ with |f(x) − f(y)| ≤ L|x − y| for x, y ∈ U, and t ∈ ℝ.

1. (The set A_t.) Let A_t := {x | x ∈ U ∧ f x < t} = U ∩ f⁻¹((−∞,t)). Since f is Lipschitz, hence continuous, on U and U is open, A_t is open (`ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage`), in particular Borel.

2. (Restriction of T.) Apply the sibling `slicing_mass_representation` to X := T (degree m+1; its hypothesis M_W(T) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U is the first half of ours). It gives μ, v with IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v and, by its conclusion (e) for the Borel set A_t, a current A ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with A(η) = ∫_{A_t} v(x)(η(x)) dμ(x) for every η ∈ D^{m+1}(U). Hence IsRestriction T A_t A (A_t is measurable; witnesses μ, v).

3. (Restriction of ∂T.) Apply the same sibling to X := ∂T (degree m; M_W(∂T) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U is the second half of our hypothesis). It gives μ′, v′ with IsMeasureRepresentation ∂T μ′ v′ and a current B ∈ D_m(U) with B(ω) = ∫_{A_t} v′(x)(ω(x)) dμ′(x) for every ω ∈ D^m(U). Hence IsRestriction ∂T A_t B.

4. (The slice.) The boundary ∂A ∈ D_m(U), ∂A(ω) = A(dω), is a current (d maps D^m(U) linearly and sequentially continuously into D^{m+1}(U); this is `GeometricCurrentOn.boundary`). Define S(ω) := ∂A(ω) − B(ω) for ω ∈ D^m(U). S is linear, and if ω_j → 0 in D^m(U) then ∂A(ω_j) → 0 and B(ω_j) → 0, so S(ω_j) → 0. Thus S ∈ D_m(U), i.e. S := ⟨toCurrent := ∂A − B, continuity from the two continuity properties⟩.

5. (Conclusion.) With the witnesses A and B of steps 2–3 and S(ω) = A.boundary(ω) − B(ω) for every ω, IsSlice T f t S holds, i.e. S = ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t} (Simon 4.6). ∎
proof_key_steps: A_t = {x ∈ U : f x < t} is open (f continuous on the open set U), hence measurable.
slicing_mass_representation for T gives a representation (μ, v) and a current A with A(η) = ∫_{A_t} v(η) dμ, so IsRestriction T A_t A.
slicing_mass_representation for ∂T gives (μ′, v′) and B with IsRestriction ∂T A_t B.
S := ∂A − B is linear and sequentially continuous, so it is a current; IsSlice T f t S with witnesses A, B.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.8 and the parent proof's Step 2 (a)–(c), with the parent's locality R4 replaced by the sibling `slicing_representation_unique` (applied to the representations supplied by IsSlice). Let P, m, U open, T ∈ D_{m+1}(U), f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz on U, t ∈ ℝ and S ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t S. Write A_t := {x | x ∈ U ∧ f x < t}.

0. (Unpacking IsSlice.) There are currents A ∈ D_{m+1}(U), B ∈ D_m(U), Borel measures μ, μ′ and maps v, v′ with: IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v and A(η) = ∫_{A_t} v(η) dμ for all η ∈ D^{m+1}(U); IsMeasureRepresentation ∂T μ′ v′ and B(ω) = ∫_{A_t} v′(ω) dμ′ for all ω ∈ D^m(U); and S(ω) = ∂A(ω) − B(ω) = A(dω) − B(ω). Since tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω (`tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset`), for every ω ∈ D^m(U):
 (*) S(ω) = ∫_{A_t} v(x)(dω(x)) dμ − ∫_{A_t} v′(x)(ω(x)) dμ′, with T(dω) = ∫ v(dω) dμ = ∂T(ω) = ∫ v′(ω) dμ′.

1. (What must be shown.) S.support = U ∖ zeroRegion(S), where zeroRegion(S) is the union of the open sets W′ with compact closure ⊆ U on which S vanishes (S(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W′). Let x ∈ S.support: x ∈ U and S vanishes on no open W′ ∋ x with compact closure ⊆ U. We show x ∈ T.support and f(x) = t by exhibiting, in each contrary case, such a W′ ∋ x on which S vanishes.

3. (f(x) = t; parent Step 2(a),(b).) f is continuous at x (continuous on the open set U ∋ x).
 (a) If f(x) < t, there is r > 0 with B(x,r) ⊆ U and f < t on B(x,r). Let W′ := B(x, r/2); it is open, its closure is the closed ball of radius r/2, compact and ⊆ B(x,r) ⊆ U. So S vanishes on W′ ∋ x, a contradiction.
 (b) If f(x) > t, there is r > 0 with B(x,r) ⊆ U and f > t on B(x,r); let W′ := B(x, r/2) as before. If tsupport ω ⊆ W′, then tsupport dω and tsupport ω are disjoint from A_t, so both integrands in (*) vanish on A_t and S(ω) = 0 − 0 = 0. Again a contradiction.
 Hence f(x) = t.

4. (Conclusion.) Every x ∈ S.support lies in T.support ∩ {x | f x = t}, i.e. spt S ⊆ spt T ∩ {f = t} (Simon 4.8). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsSlice: S(ω) = ∫_{A_t} v(dω) dμ − ∫_{A_t} v′(ω) dμ′ with representations (μ, v) of T and (μ′, v′) of ∂T.
If T vanishes on an open W′ ⊂⊂ U, so does ∂T; slicing_representation_unique with the zero representation kills both restricted integrals for forms supported in W′, so S vanishes on W′.
If f(x) < t, on a small ball inside {f < t} both restricted integrals equal T(dω), so S vanishes there.
If f(x) > t, on a small ball inside {f > t} both restricted integrals vanish, so S vanishes there.
Hence every point of spt S lies in spt T and has f = t.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.9–4.11 (pp. 157–158), including the closing sentence “To handle general Lipschitz f we simply use f^{(σ)} in place of f … then let σ ↓ 0”, i.e. the parent proof's Steps 3–4, with the parent's errata: (i) the right side of 4.10 is M_W(T⌞{a<f<b}) (printed M(T⌞{a<f<b})); (ii) ess sup_W|Df| is used as “any L_W ≥ |Df| a.e. on W”; (iii) in 4.11 “the first part of 4.11” reads “the first part of 4.9”; (iv) the argument is written for the slice ⟨T,f,t₋⟩ of 4.6. Products in [0,∞] use 0·∞ = 0.

Setting. P, m, U open; T ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure ⊆ U; f : ℝ^P → ℝ with |f(x) − f(y)| ≤ L|x−y| for x, y ∈ U; S : ℝ → D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t (S t) for every t; W ⊆ U open; L_W ≥ 0 with ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ L_W for Lebesgue-a.e. x ∈ W (Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x); a < b; R ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with IsRestriction T A_ab R, A_ab := {x | x ∈ U ∧ a < f x ∧ f x < b}.

1. (Normalized representation of T.) Apply `slicing_mass_representation` to X := T (degree m+1).  (**) |T(η)| = |∫ T⃗(x)(η(x)) dμ_T| ≤ ∫ |η(x)| dμ_T(x).

2. (Identification of R, R2.) IsRestriction T A_ab R gives that A_ab is measurable and a pair (μ_R, v_R) with IsMeasureRepresentation T μ_R v_R and R(η) = ∫_{A_ab} v_R(η) dμ_R for all η. Both pairs represent T, so ∫ v_R(η) dμ_R = T(η) = ∫ T⃗(η) dμ_T for every η ∈ D^{m+1}(U); `slicing_representation_unique` (degree m+1, open set ℝ^P) gives ∫_{A_ab} v_R(η) dμ_R = ∫_{A_ab} T⃗(η) dμ_T, i.e. R(η) = ∫_{A_ab} T⃗(η) dμ_T for all η. By step 1 (with A := A_ab, Y := R, W′ := W), M_W(R) = μ_T(W ∩ A_ab) =: Q ∈ [0,∞].

3. (Auxiliary facts.)
 (i) (McShane, `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`.) There is f̃ : ℝ^P → ℝ, L-Lipschitz on ℝ^P, with f̃ = f on U. For σ > 0 let f_σ := ρ_σ * f̃; f_σ is smooth on ℝ^P and |f_σ − f̃| ≤ Lσ everywhere.
 (ii) (Rademacher, `LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem` for the open set U.) f is differentiable at a.e. point of U, and since f̃ = f near every point of U, Df̃ = Df there. With the hypothesis: for a.e. z ∈ W, f̃ is differentiable at z and ‖Df̃(z)‖ ≤ L_W.
 (iii) (Gradient bound.) Let K ⊆ W be compact and δ₀ > 0 with the closed 2δ₀-neighbourhood K_{2δ₀} of K contained in W. For 0 < σ < δ₀, x ∈ K and a unit vector e: (f_σ(x+se) − f_σ(x))/s = ∫ ρ_σ(y)(f̃(x+se−y) − f̃(x−y))/s dy; the integrand is bounded by Lρ_σ(y) and, for 0 < |s| < δ₀, x − y ∈ K_{2δ₀} ⊆ W for |y| ≤ σ, so by (ii) (the exceptional set is Lebesgue-null and Lebesgue measure is translation invariant) it converges to ρ_σ(y)Df̃(x−y)e for a.e. y as s → 0. By dominated convergence Df_σ(x)e = ∫ ρ_σ(y)Df̃(x−y)e dy, hence |Df_σ(x)e| ≤ L_W. So ‖Df_σ(x)‖ ≤ L_W for x ∈ K.
 (iv) (R5.) For a 1-covector α and an m-covector γ, |α∧γ| ≤ |α||γ|: if α ≠ 0 choose an orthonormal basis ε₁,…,ε_P with α = |α|ε₁*; the Euclidean coefficient norm is the norm of the inner product induced on covectors, so it may be computed in this basis; writing γ = Σ_β c_β ε^β, α∧γ = |α|Σ_{β ∌ 1} c_β ε^1∧ε^β with pairwise distinct multi-indices, so |α∧γ|² = |α|²Σ_{β∌1}c_β² ≤ |α|²|γ|². For smooth g, |dg(x)| = ‖Dg(x)‖.
 (v) (Cut-offs.) For h > 0 and ε > 0 there is a smooth nonincreasing χ = χ_{h,ε} : ℝ → [0,1] with χ = 1 on (−∞, t−h], χ = 0 on [t,∞) and |χ′| ≤ (1+ε)/h (mollify, with radius < κ, the piecewise linear function equal to 1 on (−∞, t−h+κ], to 0 on [t−κ,∞) and linear in between, κ > 0 small); then χ′ = 0 outside (t−h, t).

4. (Pointwise bound 4.9, for every t ∈ ℝ.) Fix t. IsSlice T f t (S t) gives currents A, B, a representation (μ, v) of T and a representation (μ′, v′) of ∂T such that A(η) = ∫_{A_t} v(η) dμ, B(ω) = ∫_{A_t} v′(ω) dμ′ and (S t)(ω) = A(dω) − B(ω), where A_t := {x ∈ U : f(x) < t}. Fix ω admissible for M_W(S t): ω ∈ D^m(U), K := tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1. If K = ∅ then (S t)(ω) = 0; otherwise choose δ₀ as in 3(iii). Fix h > 0, ε > 0, χ := χ_{h,ε} and 0 < σ < δ₀.
 (4a) (4.11.) χ∘f_σ is smooth, so χ(f_σ)ω ∈ D^m(U) with tsupport ⊆ K, and d(χ(f_σ)ω) = χ′(f_σ)df_σ∧ω + χ(f_σ)dω with both terms in D^{m+1}(U), tsupport ⊆ K. Hence ∂T(χ(f_σ)ω) − T(χ(f_σ)dω) = T(χ′(f_σ)df_σ∧ω).
 (4b) By the representations from IsSlice, ∂T(χ(f_σ)ω) = ∫ χ(f_σ)v′(ω) dμ′ and T(χ(f_σ)dω) = ∫ χ(f_σ)v(dω) dμ.
 (4c) By (**), (iv) and (iii): |T(χ′(f_σ)df_σ∧ω)| ≤ ∫ |χ′(f_σ)||df_σ||ω| dμ_T ≤ ((1+ε)/h)·L_W·μ_T(K ∩ {t−h < f_σ < t}) ≤ ((1+ε)/h)·L_W·μ_T(K ∩ {x ∈ U : t−h−Lσ < f(x) < t+Lσ}), because χ′(f_σ(x)) ≠ 0 only if t−h < f_σ(x) < t, and |f_σ − f| ≤ Lσ on K ⊆ U.
 (4d) Let σ ↓ 0. f_σ → f̃ uniformly on ℝ^P, so χ(f_σ) → χ(f̃) uniformly; the integrands v′(ω), v(dω) are integrable and vanish off K; by dominated convergence the two integrals in (4b) converge to ∫ χ(f̃)v′(ω) dμ′ and ∫ χ(f̃)v(dω) dμ (χ∘f̃ is continuous on ℝ^P, and f̃ = f on K ⊆ U). As σ ↓ 0 the sets K ∩ {x ∈ U : t−h−Lσ < f(x) < t+Lσ} decrease, their intersection is contained in K ∩ {x ∈ U : t−h ≤ f(x) ≤ t} (with equality if L > 0), and μ_T(K) < ∞; hence lim_{σ↓0} μ_T(K ∩ {t−h−Lσ < f < t+Lσ}) ≤ μ_T(K ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}). Hence
 |∫ χ(f̃)v′(ω) dμ′ − ∫ χ(f̃)v(dω) dμ| ≤ ((1+ε)/h)·L_W·μ_T(K ∩ {x ∈ U : t−h ≤ f(x) ≤ t}).
 (4e) Let h ↓ 0 (with χ = χ_{h,ε}). For x ∈ U, χ_{h,ε}(f̃(x)) = χ_{h,ε}(f(x)) → 1_{A_t}(x) (it equals 1 once h < t − f(x) if f(x) < t, and 0 if f(x) ≥ t); the integrands vanish off K ⊆ U; by dominated convergence the left side tends to |B(ω) − A(dω)| = |(S t)(ω)|. Therefore |(S t)(ω)| ≤ liminf_{h↓0} ((1+ε)/h)·L_W·μ_T(K ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}). If L_W = 0 every term is 0 (μ_T(K) < ∞), so (S t)(ω) = 0. If L_W > 0, since K ⊆ W this is ≤ (1+ε)·L_W·Λ(t), where
 Λ(t) := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹·μ_T(W ∩ {x ∈ U : t−h ≤ f(x) ≤ t}) ∈ [0,∞].
 (4f) Letting ε ↓ 0 and taking the supremum over admissible ω (M_W(S t) is the supremum of ofReal((S t)(ω)) ≤ |(S t)(ω)|):
 (4.9) M_W(S t) ≤ L_W·Λ(t) for every t ∈ ℝ; in particular M_W(S t) = 0 for every t if L_W = 0.

5. (Measurable majorant and 4.10.)
 Case L_W = 0: g :≡ 0 is measurable; M_W(S t) = 0 = g(t) by (4.9); ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g = 0 ≤ L_W·M_W(R).
 Case L_W > 0 and Q = ∞: g :≡ ∞ is measurable, M_W(S t) ≤ g(t), and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ ∞ = L_W·Q = L_W·M_W(R).
 Case L_W > 0 and Q < ∞: let G(s) := μ_T(W ∩ {x ∈ U : a < f(x) ≤ s}) for s ∈ ℝ. G is nondecreasing, G = 0 on (−∞, a], G(s) ≤ Q < ∞ for s < b, and G is right-continuous on (−∞, b) (continuity from above for the decreasing sets W ∩ {a < f ≤ s′}, s′ ↓ s, of finite measure). For t ∈ (a,b) and k > 0 let Δ_t(k) := (G(t) − G(t−k))/k and D(t) := liminf_{k↓0} Δ_t(k) ∈ [0,∞]. Define g(t) := L_W·D(t) for t ∈ (a,b) and g(t) := 0 otherwise.
 (5a) Λ(t) ≤ D(t) for t ∈ (a,b): for h > 0 with h + h² < t − a and k := h + h², {t−h ≤ f ≤ t} ⊆ {t−k < f ≤ t}, so h⁻¹μ_T(W ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}) ≤ h⁻¹(G(t) − G(t−k)) = (1+h)Δ_t(k). Choose k_j ↓ 0 with Δ_t(k_j) → D(t) and h_j > 0 with h_j + h_j² = k_j; then h_j ↓ 0 and Λ(t) ≤ liminf_j h_j⁻¹μ_T(W ∩ {t−h_j ≤ f ≤ t}) ≤ lim_j (1+h_j)Δ_t(k_j) = D(t).
 (5b) g is Borel: for t ∈ (a,b), k ↦ G(t−k) is left-continuous on (0,∞) (right-continuity of G at t − k < b, and G = 0 on (−∞,a] with G(s) → 0 as s ↓ a), so Δ_t is left-continuous and its infimum over (0,1/j) equals its infimum over ℚ ∩ (0,1/j). Thus D(t) = sup_j inf_{q∈ℚ∩(0,1/j)} Δ_t(q), and each t ↦ Δ_t(q) is Borel on (a,b) (G is monotone on (−∞, b), hence Borel). Hence D, and g, are Borel measurable.
 (5c) For t ∈ (a,b): M_W(S t) ≤ L_W·Λ(t) ≤ L_W·D(t) = g(t), by (4.9) and (5a).
 (5d) Let a < a′ < b′ < b and G̃(s) := G(min(max(s,a′),b′)), a real-valued monotone function on ℝ. By Lebesgue's theorem (`Monotone.ae_differentiableAt`), G̃ is differentiable at a.e. s; at such s ∈ (a′,b′), G̃ = G near s, so Δ_s(k) → deriv G̃(s) and D(s) = deriv G̃(s). By `MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv` and `MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc`, deriv G̃ ≥ 0 is integrable on [a′,b′] with ∫_{a′}^{b′} deriv G̃ ≤ G̃(b′) − G̃(a′) ≤ Q. Hence ∫⁻_{(a′,b′)} D ≤ Q, and by monotone convergence (a′ ↓ a, b′ ↑ b) ∫⁻_{(a,b)} D ≤ Q. Therefore ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g = L_W·∫⁻_{(a,b)} D ≤ L_W·Q = L_W·M_W(R).

6. (Conclusion.) In every case g : ℝ → [0,∞] is measurable, M_W(S t) ≤ g(t) for all t ∈ (a,b), and ∫⁻_{t∈(a,b)} g(t) ≤ L_W·M_W(R). (This is 4.10 in its upper-integral form with M_W(T⌞{a<f<b}) on the right.) ∎

McShane extension, mollification f_σ = ρ_σ * f̃ and Rademacher give |Df_σ| ≤ L_W near tsupport ω ⊆ W.
4.11 with cut-offs χ_h: ∂T(χ(f_σ)ω) − T(χ(f_σ)dω) = T(χ′(f_σ)df_σ∧ω), bounded by ((1+ε)/h) L_W μ_T(K ∩ {t−h−Lσ < f < t+Lσ}); restriction terms evaluated in the IsSlice representations.
σ ↓ 0, then h ↓ 0 (dominated convergence), then ε ↓ 0 and sup over ω: M_W(S t) ≤ L_W · liminf_h h⁻¹ μ_T(W ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}) for every t (4.9).

subproblems.title: Slices of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity a.e. (Simon 4.1–4.5)
subproblems.statement: For all P, m, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞ for all open W ⊂⊂ U and every f : ℝ^P → ℝ which is L-Lipschitz on U: if T is integer multiplicity, then for L¹-almost every t ∈ ℝ every S ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t S is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → T.massOn W < ∞ ∧ T.boundary.massOn W < ∞) → ∀ (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0), LipschitzOnWith L f U → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn U m, IsSlice T f t S → IsIntegerMultiplicity S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions (as in the parent proof). D^k(U) is the space of test k-forms on U (smooth, compact support, tsupport ⊆ U; `TestFormOn U k`), D_k(U) the currents (`GeometricCurrentOn U k`: linear, and X(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in D^k(U), i.e. all tsupports lie in one compact K ⊆ U and every iterated derivative of ω_j tends to 0 uniformly on K). I(k,P) is the set of strictly increasing β : {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; e_β := (e_{β_1},…,e_{β_k}); dx^β is the coordinate k-covector, dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ} for β, γ ∈ I(k,P). Fact A: every k-covector α equals Σ_β α(e_β) dx^β, and |α|² = Σ_β α(e_β)², where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. A k-vector is a continuous linear functional w on k-covectors (`NVector`); put w^β := w(dx^β), so w(α) = Σ_β α(e_β) w^β and |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w| with |w| := (Σ_β (w^β)²)^{1/2} (Cauchy–Schwarz). For a form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of X(ω) over ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. ρ_ε is a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, supported in the closed ε-ball, ∫ρ_ε = 1); for a continuous compactly supported form φ, ρ_ε*φ (componentwise convolution) is smooth, supported in the closed ε-neighbourhood of tsupport φ, satisfies |ρ_ε*φ(x)| ≤ ‖φ‖ (|·| is a norm, hence convex) and ρ_ε*φ → φ uniformly as ε ↓ 0. All measures are Borel measures on ℝ^P = Eucl P.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1, Remark 4.2, 4.3, Definition 4.4 and Lemma 4.5(2) with its printed proof (pp. 154–157), i.e. the parent proof's Steps 5–7, adapted so that the conclusion holds for every S with IsSlice T f t S: the restriction terms are evaluated in the representations supplied by IsSlice, and the exceptional null set depends only on (M, θ, ξ), f and a fixed countable family of forms. Book n = m+1. The Ch. 3 results used (1.6, 1.8, 1.9, 2.10 and the co-area formula of §2) are applied on M ∩ U_i for open U_i ⊂⊂ U exhausting U, since θ is integrable only on compact subsets of U; weighted tangent spaces are local. Hⁿ = μHE[n].

Setting. P, m, U open, n := m+1, T ∈ D_n(U) with M_W(T), M_W(∂T) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U, f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz on U, and T integer multiplicity: there are M, θ, ξ with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ (M ⊆ U Hⁿ-measurable and countably n-rectifiable; θ > 0 on M and integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U; ξ Hⁿ-measurable on M and, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_n for an orthonormal basis τ of the weighted approximate tangent space T_xM of (M, θ)), θ(x) ∈ {1,2,…} for x ∈ M, and T(η) = ∫_M θ⟨η, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for η ∈ D^n(U), where ⟨η, ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(η(x)).

1. (Lipschitz extension.) By McShane (`LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`) there is an L-Lipschitz f̃ : ℝ^P → ℝ with f̃ = f on U. Since A_t := {x | x ∈ U ∧ f x < t} = {x | x ∈ U ∧ f̃ x < t}, IsSlice T f t S ⟺ IsSlice T f̃ t S for all t and S, and M ⊆ U; so it suffices to prove the claim for f̃, and we write f for f̃ (Lipschitz on all of ℝ^P).

2. (Slicing of M, Lemma 4.1 and Remark 4.2.) Let ∇^Mf be the tangential gradient (Simon Ch. 3, 2.1; defined Hⁿ-a.e. on M via the C¹ decomposition M = M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} M_j, pairwise disjoint, Hⁿ(M₀) = 0, M_j ⊆ N_j embedded C¹ n-submanifolds; |∇^Mf| ≤ L), M₊ := {x ∈ M : ∇^Mf(x) ≠ 0} and M_t := f⁻¹(t) ∩ M₊. Lemma 4.1 (printed proof: (1) is Ch. 3, 2.10(2); (2) follows from Ch. 3, 1.6 together with ∇^Mf(x) ∈ T_xM and ⟨∇^Mf(x), τ⟩ = 0 for τ ∈ T_xM_t; the last part is the co-area formula of Ch. 3, §2): for L¹-a.e. t, M_t is countably (n−1)-rectifiable and Hⁿ⁻¹-measurable, and for Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. x ∈ M_t both T_xM_t and T_xM exist, T_xM_t ⊆ T_xM is (n−1)-dimensional and T_xM = T_xM_t ⊕ ℝ∇^Mf(x); and for every nonnegative Hⁿ-measurable g on M, ∫_{−∞}^{∞}∫_{M_t} g dHⁿ⁻¹ dt = ∫_M |∇^Mf| g dHⁿ. Remark 4.2: applying this to g·1_{f<s} shows that s ↦ ∫_{M∩{f<s}} |∇^Mf| g dHⁿ = ∫_{−∞}^{s} (∫_{M_r} g dHⁿ⁻¹) dr is absolutely continuous with derivative ∫_{M_s} g dHⁿ⁻¹ for L¹-a.e. s; for Hⁿ-integrable signed g on M split g = g⁺ − g⁻. Also ∫_{M∩{f=c}} |∇^Mf| dHⁿ = ∫ Hⁿ⁻¹(M_r ∩ {f = c}) dr = 0, so ∇^Mf = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. on each level set M ∩ {f = c}.

3. (The integer multiplicity slice, 4.3–4.4.) For the L¹-a.e. t of step 2 define, for x ∈ M_t, ξ_t(x) := ξ(x)⌞(∇^Mf(x)/|∇^Mf(x)|) (interior product: ⟨ξ⌞w, α⟩ := ⟨ξ, w*∧α⟩ for (n−1)-covectors α, w* the 1-covector dual to w), ξ_t := 0 off M_t, and θ_t := θ. By 4.3, ξ_t(x) is a unit simple (n−1)-vector orienting T_xM_t for Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. x ∈ M_t: if ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_n with τ_n = ∇^Mf/|∇^Mf| and τ₁,…,τ_{n−1} an orthonormal basis of T_xM_t, then ξ_t(x) = ±(−1)^{n−1}τ₁∧⋯∧τ_{n−1}. Define ⟨T,f,t⟩(ω) := ∫_{M_t} θ_t⟨ω, ξ_t⟩ dHⁿ⁻¹ = tauAction m M_t θ_t ξ_t ω (Definition 4.4). There is an L¹-null set F₀ such that for t ∉ F₀ the triple satisfies IsRectifiableTriple U m M_t θ_t ξ_t and θ_t ∈ {1,2,…} on M_t:
 (i) M_t ⊆ M ⊆ U is Hⁿ⁻¹-measurable and countably (n−1)-rectifiable (step 2); moreover, since θ ≥ 1 on M_t and, by (iii) below, Hⁿ⁻¹(M_t ∩ K_i) ≤ ∫_{M_t∩K_i} θ dHⁿ⁻¹ < ∞ for every i, M_t is σ-finite for Hⁿ⁻¹, and an Hⁿ⁻¹-measurable σ-finite set differs from a Borel set by an Hⁿ⁻¹-null set (Borel regularity of Hausdorff measure), i.e. NullMeasurableSet M_t μHE[m];
 (ii) θ_t = θ ∈ {1,2,…} on M_t, in particular > 0;
 (iii) local integrability: choose compacts K_i ⊆ U with K_i ⊆ int K_{i+1}, ⋃K_i = U; by the co-area formula ∫∫_{M_t∩K_i} θ dHⁿ⁻¹ dt = ∫_{M∩K_i} |∇^Mf| θ dHⁿ ≤ L∫_{M∩K_i} θ dHⁿ < ∞, so for a.e. t every ∫_{M_t∩K_i} θ dHⁿ⁻¹ is finite, hence θ_t is integrable on M_t ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U;
 (iv) measurability of ξ_t and of θ_t on M_t for a.e. t (needed for `aestronglyMeasurable` and `integrableOn`): ∇^Mf, ξ and θ are Hⁿ-measurable on M; restrictions of Hⁿ-measurable functions on M to the slices M_t are Hⁿ⁻¹-measurable for a.e. t, by the co-area formula applied to the indicator functions of the Hⁿ-null sets where measurable modifications differ;
 (v) orientation: the properties “T_xM exists and ξ(x) = ±(orthonormal frame of T_xM)” hold outside an Hⁿ-null set Z ⊆ M; by the co-area formula ∫ Hⁿ⁻¹(Z ∩ M_t) dt = ∫_Z |∇^Mf| dHⁿ = 0, so for a.e. t they hold Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. on M_t, and then 4.3 applies Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. on M_t. Since θ_t is a positive integer-valued locally integrable function on the countably (n−1)-rectifiable M_t, by Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 and Remark 1.8(1) the weighted approximate tangent space of (M_t, θ_t) exists Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. on M_t and equals T_xM_t, which ξ_t orients (ξ_t(x) = ±simpleNVector of an orthonormal basis of it). (For n = 1, M_t is countable and locally finite, the weighted tangent space at each of its points is {0}, and ξ_t = ±1.)
 Moreover, for t ∉ F₀ and every compact K ⊆ U, |⟨T,f,t⟩(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖·∫_{M_t∩K} θ dHⁿ⁻¹ whenever tsupport ω ⊆ K (|⟨ω, ξ_t⟩| ≤ |ω| since ξ_t(x) is a unit simple vector).

4. (Lemma 4.5(2) for an arbitrary S.) First the printed (1): for Lipschitz h on ℝ^P with mollifications h^{(σ)} := ρ_σ*h and any bounded Hⁿ-measurable vector field Y on M vanishing outside a compact subset of U,
 (1) ∫_M θ Y·∇^M h^{(σ)} dHⁿ → ∫_M θ Y·∇^M h dHⁿ as σ ↓ 0
(the printed “weak convergence in L²(μ_T)”, localized because θ is only locally integrable). Proof: |∇^M h^{(σ)}| ≤ Lip(h) and θ is integrable on the compact set outside which Y vanishes, so by dominated convergence over j it suffices to treat Y vanishing off M_j ⊆ N_j, where ∇^M = ∇^{N_j} Hⁿ-a.e. Cover N_j by countably many C¹ charts φ : Ω → N_j and split M_j accordingly.
